source_text: Κυβερνήτην μὲν γὰρ ὁ χειμὼν, καὶ τὸν ἀθλητὴν τὸ στάδιον, τὸν στρατηγὸν ἡ παράταξις, τὸν μεγαλόψυχον ἡ συμφορὰ, τὸν Χριστιανὸν δὲ πειρασμὸς δοκιμάζει καὶ βασανίζει. Καὶ αἱ λύπαι τὴν ψυχὴν, ὡς τὸ πῦρ τὸν χρυσὸν, ἀπελέγχουσι. Πένης εἶ; Μὴ ἀθυμήσῃς. Ἡ γὰρ εἰς ἄγαν κατήφεια γίνεται τῆς ἁμαρτίας αἰτία· τῆς μὲν λύπης βαπτιζούσης τὸν νοῦν, καὶ ἀμηχανίας ἐμποιούσης ἴλιγγον, τῆς δὲ ἀπορίας τῶν λογισμῶν τὴν ἀχαριστίαν ἀπογεννώσης. Ἀλλ' ἔχε τὴν ἐλπίδα πρὸς τὸν Θεόν. Μὴ γὰρ οὐκ ἐπιβλέπει τὴν στένωσιν; Ἔχει τὴν τροφὴν ἐν χερσὶ, καὶ παρέλκει τὴν δόσιν, ἵνα σου δοκιμάσῃ τὸ βέβαιον, ἵνα καταμάθῃ τὴν γνώμην, εἰ μὴ τῇ τῶν ἀκολάστων καὶ ἀγνωμόνων ἐστὶν ὁμοία. Καὶ γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι, μέχρι μὲν ἐν τῷ στόματι τὰ σιτία τυγχάνει, εὐφημοῦσι, κολακεύουσιν, ὑπερθαυμάζουσιν· ὀλίγον δὲ τῆς τραπέζης ὑπερτεθείσης, ὥσπερ τισὶ λίθοις ταῖς βλασφημίαις βάλλουσιν οὓς πρὸ βραχέως ἴσα Θεῷ διὰ τὴν ἡδονὴν προσεκύνουν. Ἔπελθε τὴν Παλαιὰν Διαθή κην, τὴν Νέαν, καὶ πολλοὺς εὑρήσεις ἐν ἑκάστῃ τοὺς διαφόρως τραφέντας. Ἠλίαν εἶχεν ὁ Κάρμηλος, ὄρος ὑψηλὸν καὶ ἀοίκητον, ἔρημος ἔρημον· ψυχὴ δὲ ἦν τῷ δικαίῳ τὰ πάντα, καὶ τῆς ζωῆς ἐφόδιον ἡ πρὸς Θεὸν ἐλπίς. Ζῶν δὲ οὕτω, λιμῷ τὴν ζωὴν οὐκ ἀπήλλαξεν· ἀλλ' οἱ ἁρπακτικώτατοι καὶ μάλιστα γαστρίμαργοι τῶν ὀρνίθων, οὗτοι διεκόμιζον τὰ σιτία, καὶ τροφῆς ἐγίνοντο τῷ δικαίῳ διάκονοι, οἱ τὰς ἀλλοτρίας τροφὰς ἐκ συνηθείας ἁρπάζοντες· καὶ τῷ δεσποτικῷ προστάγματι τὴν φύσιν διήμειψαν, πιστοὶ φύλακες γενόμενοι τῶν ἄρτων καὶ τῶν κρεῶν. Ταῦτα δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ φέρειν τοὺς κόρακας παρὰ τῆς πνευματικῆς ἱστορίας ἐμάθομεν. Εἶχε δὲ καὶ ὁ Βαβυλώνιος λάκκος τὸν Ἰσραηλίτην νεανίσκον· αἰχμάλωτον μὲν τὴν συμ φορὰν, ἐλεύθερον δὲ τὴν ψυχὴν καὶ τὸ φρόνημα. Καὶ τί τὰ παρ' ἐκείνων; Οἱ μὲν λέοντες παρὰ φύσιν ἐνήστευον· ὁ δὲ τούτου τροφεὺς Ἀμβακοὺμ ἐφέρετο δι' ἀέρος, κομίζοντος τοῦ ἀγγέλου μετὰ τῶν ὄψων τὸν ἄνθρωπον· καὶ ἵνα μὴ λιμῷ πιεσθῇ δίκαιος, τοσαύτης ὑπερηνέχθη γῆς καὶ θαλάσσης ὁ προφήτης ἐν μικρῷ μορίῳ καιροῦ, ὅσην ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας μέχρι Βαβυλῶνος ἡπλῶσθαι. Τί δὲ πάλιν ὁ τῆς ἐρήμου λαὸς, οὗ Μωϋσῆς ἐπετρόπευσε; πῶς ᾠκονομήθη τὸν βίον ἐν ἔτεσι τεσσαράκοντα; Οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ σπείρων ἀνὴρ, οὐ βοῦς ἕλκων ἄροτρον, οὐχ ἅλως, οὐ ληνὸς, οὐ ταμιεῖον· καὶ τὴν τροφὴν εἶχον ἄσπορον καὶ ἀνήροτον, καὶ τὰς πη γὰς ἐχορήγει πέτρα, οὐ πρότερον οὔσας, ἀλλ' ἐκραγείσας ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας, Ἀφίημι τὰ καθ' ἕκαστον ἀπ αριθμεῖσθαι τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ προνοίας, ἃ πολλάκις ἐπὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων πατρικῶς ἐνεδείξατο. Σὺ δὲ καρτέρη σον ὀλίγον ἐπὶ τῆς συμφορᾶς, ὡς ὁ γενναῖος Ἰὼβ, καὶ μὴ περιτραπῇς ἐκ τοῦ κλύδωνος, μηδὲν ἀποβά λῃς ὧν φέρεις ἀγωγίμων τῆς ἀρετῆς. Ὡς βαρύτιμον ἐνθήκην τὴν εὐχαριστίαν διάσωσον ἐπὶ τῆς ψυχῆς, καὶ λήψῃ καὶ σὺ τῆς εὐχαριστίας τὰ διπλασίονα τῆς τρυφῆς. Μνημόνευε τῆς ἀποστολικῆς ῥήσεως· Ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε. Πένης εἶ; Ἄλλον ἔχεις πάντως πενέστερον. Σοὶ δέκα ἡμερῶν τὰ σιτία, ἐκείνῳ μιᾶς. Ὡς καλὸς καὶ εὐγνώμων τὸ σὸν περιτ τὸν ἐπανίσωσον πρὸς τὸν ἐνδεῆ.
thought_title: Trial That Proves and Feeds the Enduring
orientation: Basil is speaking to sufferers of famine to show that the present distress is a trial that proves the Christian and requires endurance hope thanksgiving and sharing.
pass_a_gloss: For the storm tests the helmsman, and the race course tests the athlete, the battle line tests the general, calamity tests the great souled man, and trial tests and examines the Christian. And sorrows prove the soul, as fire proves gold. Are you poor? Do not lose heart. For dejection carried to excess becomes cause of sin, with grief submerging the mind and producing dizziness of helplessness, and with need giving birth to ingratitude of thoughts. But hold hope toward God. For does he not look upon groaning? He holds food in hands, and he delays the giving, in order that he may test your firmness, in order that he may learn your purpose, whether it is not like that of the undisciplined and ungrateful. For those men, as long as foods happen to be in the mouth, they speak well of him, they flatter, they marvel exceedingly, but when the table has been delayed a little, as if with stones they strike with blasphemies those whom a little before for pleasure they worshiped as equal to God. Go through the Old Covenant, the New, and you will find many in each fed in different ways. Mount Carmel held Elijah, a high mountain and uninhabited, a desert place holding a desert man, and for the righteous man all things were soul, and provision of life was hope toward God. And living thus, he did not escape life from famine, but the most rapacious and most gluttonous of birds, these carried the foods, and they became servants of food to the righteous man, they who seize the foods of others from habit, and by the command of the master they exchanged nature, since they became faithful guardians of the loaves and the meats. And that the ravens bring these things to the man we learned from the spiritual history. And the lions' den in Babylon held the Israelite young man, captive in calamity, but free in soul and in mind. And what are the things that came from those men? The lions fasted contrary to nature, and Habakkuk, feeder of this man, was carried through air, with the angel carrying the man with the cooked dishes, and in order that a righteous man might not be pressed by famine, the prophet was lifted above so much land and sea in a small portion of time, as much as stretches from Judea as far as Babylon. And what again of the people of the desert, over whom Moses was guardian? How was life managed for them in forty years? There was no man sowing there, no ox dragging a plow, no threshing floor, no wine vat, no storehouse, and they had food unsown and unplowed, and rock supplied the springs, which did not exist before, but burst out at the need. I pass over counting one by one the acts of the providence of God, which he often showed to men in a fatherly way. But you endure a little upon calamity, as noble Job did, and do not be overturned by the wave, and do not throw away any of the things conducive to virtue which you carry. As a costly deposit preserve thanksgiving upon the soul, and you also will receive for thanksgiving double luxury. Remember the apostolic saying. In everything give thanks. Are you poor? You certainly have another man poorer. For you the foods are of ten days, for that man of one day. As a good and grateful man share your excess equally with the needy.

choices.why: keeps literal sense of great soul without importing a single virtue term
marks the second verb as intensive proving distinct from tests

choices.english: a desert place holding a desert man
choices.why: preserves the stark parallel adjectives for place and for man
keeps the participle force of things leading toward virtue
renders the literal equalize your surplus toward the needy as concrete sharing

pass_b_english: A storm puts the pilot to the proof, the stadium puts the athlete to the proof, the battle line puts the general to the proof, hardship puts the great souled man to the proof, and a trial tests and examines the Christian. Sorrows prove the soul the way fire proves gold.

Are you poor? Do not lose heart. Excessive dejection leads to sin. Sorrow drowns the mind and brings on the dizziness of helplessness, and the failure of reason gives birth to ingratitude. Keep your hope in God. Does he not look upon your groaning? The food is in his hands, and he holds back the gift to test your steadfastness and to learn your resolve, whether it does not resemble that of the dissolute and ungrateful. Those people praise and flatter and marvel while the food is still in their mouths, but when the table is delayed a little they hurl blasphemies like stones at those they worshipped for pleasure as equals of God just before.

Go through the Old Testament and the New, and you will find many in each who were fed in different ways. Mount Carmel held Elijah, a high and uninhabited mountain, a desert place holding a desert man. To the righteous man the soul was everything, and hope in God was his provision for life. Though he lived in this way, famine did not take his life. The most rapacious and gluttonous of birds carried him food and became servants of his nourishment, though by habit they snatched food belonging to others. By the Master's command they changed their nature and became faithful guardians of the loaves and the meat. We learn from the spiritual history that ravens brought these things to the man.

The lions' den in Babylon held the Israelite young man, captive in calamity but free in soul and purpose. What happened there? The lions fasted against nature, while Habakkuk, his feeder, was carried through the air, as the angel bore the man along with the dishes. So that the righteous man would not be crushed by famine, the prophet was lifted over as much land and sea as stretches from Judea to Babylon, in a small moment of time. Consider again the people in the desert whom Moses guided. How were they sustained in life for forty years? No man sowed there, no ox drew a plow, no threshing floor, no winepress, no storehouse, yet they had food that was neither sown nor plowed, and rock supplied springs that had not existed before but burst forth in their need. I will not count one by one the acts of God's providence that he has shown to human beings many times with a father's care.

Endure the calamity a little, as noble Job did, and do not let the wave overturn you, and do not throw overboard any of the cargo of virtue you carry. Preserve thanksgiving in your soul like a costly treasure chest, and you too will receive twice the luxury in return for your thanksgiving. Remember the apostle's saying: Give thanks in all circumstances (1 Thessalonians 5:18). Are you poor? You surely have someone poorer than yourself. You have food for ten days, and he has food for one. As a good and grateful man, share your excess equally with the needy.

problems.quote: whether it resembles that of the dissolute and ungrateful
problems.source_quote: εἰ μὴ τῇ τῶν ἀκολάστων καὶ ἀγνωμόνων ἐστὶν ὁμοία
problems.why: Greek has negation μὴ; English drops not, reversing whether-clause sense.
problems.fix: whether it is not like that of the dissolute and ungrateful
problems.ruling: Source has εἰ μὴ ('unless/if not... resembles'), so 'whether it resembles' drops μὴ and could reverse the sense; should read 'whether it is not like'/'that it is not like' the dissolute.

problems.source_quote: μηδὲν ἀποβάλῃς ὧν φέρεις ἀγωγίμων τῆς ἀρετῆς
problems.why: ἀγωγίμων means cargo or wares. The sense is the cargo of virtue you carry, still on the storm-tossed ship. 'Conducive to virtue' loses the image and changes the meaning.
